title: Retrospective Analysis of the VAERS Database for Novel Infant Safety Signals
content: In recent studies, novel candidate safety signals were detected for infants for specific vaccines.  Herein, the Vaccine Adverse Events Reporting System (VAERS) database was retrospectively examined for possible novel candidate safety signals for infants.  Novel candidate safety signals were detected for multiple vaccines.  Multiple safety signals were detected for live, attenuated rotavirus vaccines, the meningococcal B (Bexsero) vaccine, and concurrently administered vaccine combinations.  Candidate safety signals were detected for adverse event (AE) sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS) for two standalone administered vaccines and eighteen concurrently administered vaccine combinations.  Understanding the etiology of these candidate adverse events should enable minimizing them in current and future vaccines.  Multiple manufacturing lots with three or more SIDS AEs were identified.  An unknown factor, theta, is hypothesized to be associated with these lots.  Elimination or reduction of theta in vaccines is hypothesized to reduce SIDS AEs to background risk level.  These candidate safety signals need to be considered in the context of risks associated with vaccine target pathogens.
